correctness.rationale: For n≥4 and 0<a<1/(n−1), the path energy estimate gives positive definiteness on the orthogonal complement of the constants. The prose after the energy inequality should say the energy is zero only on constants: the comparison inequality itself has equality on every affine vertex profile, by the equality case of Cauchy–Schwarz. This imprecision does not affect the positive lower bound off constants or any conclusion. For s>0, the leading continuants p_k=U_k−U_{k−1} satisfy p_k−p_{k−1}=s U_{k−1}>0; the final endpoint diagonal gives det(sI+L_path)=s U_{n−1}. Cofactors and the rank-one inverse identity then give strict endpoint minimality of the shifted inverse. The identity p_{n−1}²−1=s U_{n−1}U_{n−2} follows from the Chebyshev recurrence and U_m²−U_{m−1}U_{m+1}=1. The endpoint resolvent has exactly one scale sign change; the positive and negative Mellin contributions have strictly ordered log-scale means, so the zero is simple and unique, with existence supplied by the spectral projection and order-one limits. At this zero the only off-diagonal pair missing from the generator graph is the closing edge, so all heat entries are still strictly positive at all positive times. Above it, the endpoint Taylor coefficient is negative; convergence to the uniform projection gives permanent eventual positivity. Differentiation is justified on compact interior parameter sets: the rank-one derivative is bounded near s=0 because the perturbing vector is orthogonal to constants, and decays as s⁻² at infinity; log factors for the order derivative are integrable. Its endpoint sign is strictly negative. At critical conductance the endpoint resolvent is strictly negative for every s>0; allowing the additional zero mode there is consistent with continuity of the fractional power for each fixed positive order. This proves the stated decreasing threshold and its two limiting values, within 0<α<1. The frozen finite rational/spectral checker was inspected, not executed, and is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The supported distinction is the explicit identification of the controlling pair and Chebyshev threshold with strict conductance dependence for every stable signed cycle in scope. The abstract existence of a threshold is not credited as a novelty: once a power is an irreducible graph Laplacian, every lower power has strictly negative off-diagonals by the ordinary fractional graph theorem; continuity and the order-zero and order-one limits give an interval of admissible orders. The sources inspected do not thereby determine the critical entry, integral, or its conductance law. No ordering is inferred between different records on the shared publication date.
residual_risks: An unindexed cycle or rank-one perturbation theorem could contain the same explicit critical-entry result; shared-date catalogue records do not establish publication priority.

value.rationale: The precise sign-controlling edge matters: it replaces an all-entry, all-time positivity test by a one-dimensional computation and locates the loss of the Markov property without recomputing heat kernels. The uniform cycle family is a natural sparse competitor to complete antagonistic networks. The root's strict conductance ordering and limits quantify how much fractionalization the signed network needs; these are not supplied by existence of a Markov interval alone. No claim is made about the last negative time above the threshold, arbitrary signed networks, or the heat limit at critical conductance.
